calls.head: Strength against strength
calls.body: The Panthers are near the top of the league for the power play, and the Hurricanes are near the top of the league at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Panthers’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots.
calls.call: The Panthers’ power play creates more than the league-average 7.6 expected goals per 60 against the Hurricanes.
calls.nums: Florida 7th for the power play (8.0 expected goals per 60) · Carolina 6th for the penalty kill
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 0 and 0 games this season
calls.happened: On the power play, Florida had 2.3 per 60. The league average is 7.6 per 60, and they came in at 8.0 per 60.

calls.head: Something has to give
calls.body: The Hurricanes are one of the league’s best for shot volume, and the Panthers are near the top of the league at keeping shots away. We think the Hurricanes still get theirs.
calls.call: The Hurricanes take more than the league-average 56.8 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5 against the Panthers.
calls.nums: Carolina 2nd for shot volume (69.9 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5) · Florida 8th for keeping shots away
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 0 and 0 games this season
calls.happened: On 5-on-5 shot attempts, Carolina had 24.1 per 60. The league average is 56.8 per 60, and they came in at 69.9 per 60.

calls.head: Active D against forward-led
calls.body: On shots from defensemen, Carolina is one of the league’s best and Florida is one of the league’s worst. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
calls.call: The Hurricanes’ defensemen take a bigger share of the team’s shot attempts than the Panthers’.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 0 and 0 games this season
calls.happened: On share of 5-on-5 shot attempts taken by defensemen, Carolina had 56% and Florida 29%. Coming in, Carolina was at 38% and Florida at 31%.

CAR.head: We gave Carolina a 69% chance, but Florida had other ideas.

FLA.head: We gave Florida a 31% chance, and Florida proved us wrong.

surprises.head: Florida brought the hits
surprises.body: Florida’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 257, against their usual 122 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 600 games.

surprises.head: Florida flipped the shot count
surprises.body: Florida took 65% of the 5-on-5 shot attempts (adjusted for score and venue). From how these two usually play, Florida would expect about 42%. A team strays this far about once every 900 games.

surprises.head: Carolina shut down Florida’s power play
surprises.body: Florida’s power play created 2.3 expected goals per 60, against their usual 8.0 and a league average of 7.6. A team strays this far about once every 35 games.

surprises.head: J. Markstrom stole one
surprises.body: J. Markstrom allowed 0 goals on shots worth 2.5 expected goals, 2.5 fewer than expected. Starting goalies had a night this good about once every 25 starts over the last three seasons.

story.head: Markstrom shuts out the Hurricanes
paras: Gustav Forsling won it in overtime. Jacob Markstrom stopped all 15 shots.
The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way.

items.text: One of the preview’s three calls held.
